feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: Brazil's big political rematch: What to know
entry.summary: Four years after President Lula narrowly defeated Jair Bolsonaro, Brazil is back at the ballot box. This time, Lula faces Bolsonaro's son, Flávio, in a high-stakes rematch.

entry.title: As Trump's proposed arch looms over D.C., protesters pin their hopes on the midterms
entry.summary: Democratic lawmakers, veterans and concerned citizens gathered in Memorial Circle to protest the arch Trump wants to build there. Their hopes lie primarily in a lawsuit and next month's midterms.

entry.title: Germany's political center fights for relevance after far-right and far-left gains
entry.summary: Centrist politicians are soul-searching after electoral gains by the far right and the far left. Today's weak coalitions, political fragmentation and dire economy echo a past that led to the rise of fascism.

entry.title: Pro-Trump Influencer Benny Johnson is being sued for defamation by ICE protesters
entry.summary: The lawsuit says the prominent conservative podcaster falsely claimed the protesters were assaulting ICE officers during demonstrations at an ICE facility in Illinois last year.

entry.title: October 1 ushered in a new era in U.S. foreign aid. What's the plan? Will it work?
entry.summary: The America First strategy asks for a Memorandum of Understanding as a condition for healthcare and development aid. It's been praised for promoting self-reliance but criticized for its conditions.

entry.title: Cloaked in anonymity, Israeli soldiers describe mass civilian killings in 'NAZA'
entry.summary: NAZA is an acronym for nezek agavi, Hebrew for "collateral damage." It refers to the number of civilian casualties the Israeli military deems acceptable. The documentary is made by Israeli filmmakers.

entry.title: The U.S. added only 29,000 jobs in September as job market lacks spark
entry.summary: U.S. employers added 29,000 jobs in September as the unemployment rate inched up to 4.2%. Job gains for July and August were revised down by a total of 60,000 jobs, extending a lackluster run for the job market.

entry.title: Cornell rape case gets special prosecutor. And, Renee Good's family sues the government
entry.summary: New legal action in two closely watched cases: one at Cornell, the other over Renee Good's death. We take a closer look.

entry.title: Why is diesel more expensive than regular gas?
entry.summary: Diesel hasn't always been more expensive than other gasoline. Then in 2004, a switch happened due to air quality standards, demand, and taxes. In this week's Indicator newsletter, we dig into diesel prices, what kind of fun people are buying, and other forms of making your tax bill smaller.

entry.title: San Francisco's car crime has plunged. How much credit does Flock deserve?
entry.summary: San Francisco leaders say AI-powered cameras helped drive a dramatic decline in car crime. We examine the evidence — and whether the city can keep its high-tech dragnet without sacrificing civil liberties.
